title: 1.3.12 Rate These Names
description: Six names, and one that is genuinely borderline. Judge each and say which rule it breaks. AI-graded with hints.

rubric.title: All six names are judged
rubric.description: Student gives a verdict on each of the six names. The verdicts should broadly match: x bad, numberOfStudents good, d bad, currentDay good, temp borderline-or-weak, bodyTemperature good. Credit requires all six addressed; a wrong call on temp alone does not lose this criterion since it is the deliberately arguable one.

rubric.title: Reasons name the rule, not just the verdict
rubric.description: For the bad names the student says WHAT is wrong in the vocabulary of the module - a single letter carries no information, the name is too vague, you cannot tell what it holds. Deny if the answers are bare verdicts ('bad', 'good') or only 'it is confusing' with no rule attached.

rubric.title: Q7: identifies temp as the borderline one, with an argument
rubric.description: Student names temp and explains the tension: it is a widely-used short form for temperature (and also for 'temporary', which is the ambiguity), so it is readable to many programmers but still less clear than bodyTemperature. Credit any answer that names temp AND gives a real reason it is arguable rather than simply bad.

rubric.title: Q8: the four problems are matched correctly
rubric.description: Expected matching: temp = too generic; x = abbreviation with no context; a1 = numbered name that says nothing; myVariable = meaningless but harmless-sounding. Credit three or four correct. Deny two or fewer.
